# Overview {.unnumbered}

Most published sequencing papers deposit their raw reads in a public
archive. Re-using them is one of the cheapest experiments in biology: a
control for your own data, a new question asked of an old dataset, or a way
to learn a pipeline. Getting the files out is less obvious than it should be.
This guide explains, from the beginning, how to go from "the paper says the data
are in GEO" to a folder of `.fastq.gz` files ready for any analysis pipeline.

It's written for wet-lab scientists who are new to the command line, and it
works on a **laptop, a workstation, or a computing cluster**. If terms like
*FASTQ*, *gzip* or *terminal* are unfamiliar, the Foundations chapters of
[omics-walkthru](https://jpflores-13.github.io/omics-walkthru) explain them.

## Choose your route

Answer these questions in order. Each box links to the chapter that covers it.

```{mermaid}

  START(["You have a paper or an accession"]) --> Q0{"Do you need the raw reads,<br/>or just the authors' results?"}
  Q0 -->|"just their results<br/>(counts, bigWigs, peaks)"| SUP["Download GEO supplementary files<br/>(plain links, no toolkit)<br/>→ The databases"]

  SRA --> Q3{"How many runs?"}

  classDef stop fill:#fdf3e7,stroke:#d98b2b;
  class SUP,CA stop;
```

## The short version

With the SRA Toolkit installed ([Setup](chapters/setup.qmd)):

```bash
prefetch SRR1039508 --max-size u               # 1. download the .sra file
vdb-validate SRR1039508                        # 2. check it
fasterq-dump SRR1039508 --threads 4 --temp tmp # 3. convert to FASTQ
pigz SRR1039508*.fastq                         # 4. compress (gzip works too)
```

That gives `SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz` and `SRR1039508_2.fastq.gz`. Or, without any
toolkit, from ENA:

```bash
wget https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz
wget https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_2.fastq.gz
```

The rest of the guide explains each of those lines, how to find the
accession, how to do it for 50 samples at once, and how to check and organise
what you got.

## The whole path, from paper to pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P["Paper<br/>'data in GEO GSE52778'"] --> G["GEO series<br/>GSE → GSM samples"]
  G --> S["SRA Run Selector / ENA<br/>GSM → SRR runs<br/>+ metadata table"]
  S --> L["SRR_Acc_List.txt<br/>SraRunTable.csv"]
  L --> PF["prefetch<br/>.sra"] --> V["vdb-validate"] --> FQ["fasterq-dump<br/>.fastq"] --> Z["pigz<br/>.fastq.gz"]
  L -. "or" .-> E["ENA<br/>.fastq.gz + MD5"]
  Z & E --> M["check counts,<br/>merge runs per sample,<br/>rename"]
  M --> B["samplesheet →<br/>your pipeline"]
```

## How this guide is organised

| Part | Chapters | Read it when |
|---|---|---|
| Concepts | [The databases](chapters/databases.qmd), [Accessions](chapters/accessions.qmd), [Finding the data](chapters/finding-data.qmd) | You have a paper and want to know what to download |
| Downloading | [Setup](chapters/setup.qmd), [prefetch](chapters/prefetch.qmd), [fasterq-dump](chapters/fasterq-dump.qmd), [Downloading many runs](chapters/at-scale.qmd) | You're ready to download |
| After the download | [Verify and organise](chapters/verify-organise.qmd), [Worked example](chapters/worked-example.qmd) | You have FASTQs and want to run a pipeline |
| Appendices | [ENA](chapters/ena.qmd), [Special cases](chapters/special-cases.qmd), [Troubleshooting](chapters/troubleshooting.qmd), [Cheat sheet](chapters/cheatsheet.qmd) | Something is unusual, or you just need the commands |

The repository's `scripts/` folder has ready-to-use scripts:

| Script | Does | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| [`scripts/download_sra.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/download_sra.sh) | prefetch → validate → fasterq-dump → compress, one run per array task | Any SLURM cluster |
| [`scripts/submit_each.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/submit_each.sh) | The same steps, as one ordinary job per run; `fasterq-dump` or `parallel-fastq-dump` | Any SLURM cluster |
| [`scripts/find_missing.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/find_missing.sh) | List runs with missing, corrupt or mismatched FASTQ, to resubmit | Anywhere |
| [`scripts/merge_runs.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/merge_runs.sh) | Combine runs of the same sample; rename to `<sample>_R1_001.fastq.gz` | Anywhere |
| [`scripts/ena_download.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/ena_download.sh) | Download ready-made `.fastq.gz` from ENA and check MD5s | Anywhere with `curl`, `wget`, `md5sum` |

::: {.callout-note}
## Running example

Throughout, we use the **airway** dataset (GEO
[GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778); Himes
*et al.*, *PLoS One* 2014): RNA-seq of human airway smooth muscle cells from
four donors, untreated or treated with dexamethasone. It's paired-end, about
20–40 million read pairs per run, and widely used for teaching (it's the
Bioconductor `airway` package). Files for it are in `examples/`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
